prompt.context_jp: 彼は物を散らかさないようにすることを何より重んじる男で、独りきりの空間こそ、彼にとって最も落ち着ける聖域なのである。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼___物を散らかさないようにすることを何より重んじる男で…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits? Kuwano is being described as a known topic.

feedback.correct_en: Kuwano has already been introduced; the sentence continues to comment on him as the ongoing topic, so は is natural.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark him as newly identified information, which clashes with the narrator's continued commentary.

contrast_examples.en: HE is the meticulous one. (identifies who)

prompt.context_jp: 診察室のドアが開き、桑野が入ってきた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 診察室のドア___開き、桑野が入ってきた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for this new event?

feedback.correct_en: The door opening is a new event being reported — scene-setting new information takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn 'the door' into a contrastive topic, which doesn't fit a sudden event.

contrast_examples.jp: ドアは開いた(が、窓は閉まっていた)。
contrast_examples.en: The door opened (but the window was closed). (contrast)

prompt.context_jp: 「それが この人の仕事ですから」
prompt.prompt_jp: それ___ この人の仕事ですから。
prompt.prompt_en: Pointing out 'THAT is what his job is' — which particle?

feedback.correct_en: The speaker is identifying 'that (understanding housewives' feelings)' as being exactly his job — an exhaustive/identifying が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 'that' an old topic, losing the pointing/identifying nuance the moment needs.

contrast_examples.en: That is a job (as for that…). (topic)

prompt.context_jp: 「あ～あ 私も嫁が欲しい」
prompt.prompt_jp: 私も嫁___欲しい。
prompt.prompt_en: With 欲しい (want), which particle marks the thing wanted?

feedback.correct_en: Adjectives of desire like 欲しい take が to mark the object of wanting.
feedback.incorrect_en: を is used with verbs like 欲しがる, not with the adjective 欲しい. は would turn 嫁 into a contrastive topic.

prompt.context_jp: 「僕はね 仕事が どんなに忙しくても 家の中が散らかってると」
prompt.prompt_jp: 僕___ね、仕事がどんなに忙しくても…
prompt.prompt_en: Kuwano is declaring his personal stance — which particle?

feedback.correct_en: 'As for me' — he's setting himself up as the topic to express his personal principle. は with ね emphasizes the topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: 僕が would sound like identifying 'I'm the one who...', which doesn't match the general statement he's making.

contrast_examples.en: As for me, I can't stand it.
I'M the one who can't stand it.

prompt.context_jp: 「僕はね 仕事が どんなに忙しくても 家の中が散らかってると」
prompt.prompt_jp: 家の中___散らかってると…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in this conditional clause?

feedback.correct_en: In subordinate 〜と conditional clauses describing a state, が marks the subject of the embedded state neutrally.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would pull the inside of the house out as a contrastive topic, breaking the flow of the conditional.

contrast_examples.jp: 部屋が散らかってると落ち着かない。
contrast_examples.en: If the room is messy, I can't relax.

contrast_examples.jp: 部屋は散らかっている。

prompt.context_jp: 「家事ができないなんて言ってる人は 結局は嫌いなんですね 家事が」
prompt.prompt_jp: 家事ができないなんて言ってる人___ 結局は嫌いなんですね 家事が。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks this generic group of people?

feedback.correct_en: 'People who say they can't do housework' is set up as a generic topic for a sweeping judgment — classic は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would narrow it to identifying specific people, undermining the general claim.

contrast_examples.en: Those kinds of people — I dislike (them).
It's those kinds of people (specifically) I dislike.

prompt.context_jp: しかし桑野の負けん気は、こういうときにこそ火がつく性質だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: しかし桑野の負けん気___、こういうときにこそ火がつく性質だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for this narrator-introduced topic?

feedback.correct_en: The narrator sets '桑野の負けん気' as the topic to then comment on its nature — は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would awkwardly flag it as new info, but the narrator is making a general characterization.

contrast_examples.en: His personality is complex. (comment on topic)

prompt.context_jp: 「家は やっぱり 彼女と過ごす場所でしょう」
prompt.prompt_jp: 家___ やっぱり 彼女と過ごす場所でしょう。
prompt.prompt_en: Eiji is giving his view on what home is. Which particle?

feedback.correct_en: Setting up '家' as a topic for a general statement about it — は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would identify home as 'the place where' among options, which doesn't fit the generic claim.

contrast_examples.en: Home is a place to relax.
Home is where I feel most at ease.

prompt.context_jp: 同じ頃、桑野の部屋の電話が鳴った。
prompt.prompt_jp: 同じ頃、桑野の部屋の電話___鳴った。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for this sudden event?

feedback.correct_en: The phone ringing is a new narrative event — が for event report.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would strangely topicalize the phone as if contrasting with something else.

prompt.context_jp: 「人にはね それぞれ 聖域というものが必要なんです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 人___はね、それぞれ聖域というものが必要なんです。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle combines with は to mean 'for people'?

feedback.correct_en: 人には = 'for people / to people' — に marks the experiencer, with は adding topic/emphasis.
feedback.incorrect_en: を doesn't fit with 必要; が wouldn't combine this way with は.

prompt.context_jp: 席を立とうとした瞬間、桑野の体が大きく傾いだ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 桑野の体___大きく傾いだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for this dramatic event?

feedback.correct_en: A sudden event being reported neutrally takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply contrast ('his body, at least, tilted'), which makes no sense here.

contrast_examples.en: His eyes, at least, were closed. (contrast)

prompt.context_jp: 「血圧も やや高めだし 2～3日は安静するようにって」
prompt.prompt_jp: 2～3日___安静するようにって。
prompt.prompt_en: 'For 2-3 days at least, rest.' Which particle gives a contrastive/limiting nuance?

feedback.correct_en: は on a time span signals 'at least this much' — a bounded, contrastive reading fitting the doctor's advice.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would awkwardly spotlight the duration as new info rather than a boundary.

contrast_examples.en: I'll rest for at least a week.

prompt.context_jp: 「愛があるかどうか この違いは大きいわよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 愛___あるかどうか、この違いは大きいわよ。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in 'whether there is love'?

feedback.correct_en: Existence verb ある takes が to mark what exists — 'whether love exists'.
feedback.incorrect_en: 愛は would set love as topic, but in this embedded existence clause we need neutral が.

prompt.context_jp: 「あの男は 大体 自分勝手なんだよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: あの男___ 大体 自分勝手なんだよ。
prompt.prompt_en: Launching a tirade about Kuwano — which particle?

feedback.correct_en: 'That man' is being set up as the topic for sweeping criticism — は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would narrow it to 'HE (of all people) is selfish', which is odd for a general character complaint.

prompt.context_jp: 「そのくせ 仕事だけは ちゃんとしてんだよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: そのくせ 仕事だけ___ ちゃんとしてんだよ。
prompt.prompt_en: 'Yet (only) his work he does properly.' Which particle?

feedback.correct_en: だけは explicitly contrasts: 'work, at least, he does right' (unlike everything else). Pure contrastive は.
feedback.incorrect_en: だけが would exhaustively identify it, losing the 'despite everything else' nuance.

contrast_examples.jp: 仕事だけはちゃんとする。
contrast_examples.en: Work, at least, he handles properly.

contrast_examples.jp: 仕事だけがうまくいく。
contrast_examples.en: Only work goes well (nothing else does).

prompt.context_jp: 招待客たちは彼の几帳面な仕事ぶりを口々に褒め…
prompt.prompt_jp: 招待客たちは彼の几帳面な仕事ぶり___口々に褒め…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks what they praised?

feedback.correct_en: 褒める is a transitive verb; its direct object is marked with を.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark a subject, and に a target/direction, neither of which fits the object of praise here.

prompt.context_jp: 深夜のコンビニに、桑野は栄養ドリンクを買いに立ち寄った。
prompt.prompt_jp: 深夜のコンビニ___、桑野は栄養ドリンクを買いに立ち寄った。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits with 立ち寄る (drop by)?

feedback.correct_en: 立ち寄る takes に to mark the destination you stop by at.
feedback.incorrect_en: で marks the location of an action, but 立ち寄る focuses on arrival at a point.

prompt.context_jp: 「家事をさせるなら 家政婦を___ば済む話だ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 家政婦を___ば済む話だ。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb collocates with 家政婦 (housekeeper)?

feedback.correct_en: 雇う is the standard verb for hiring staff like a housekeeper.
feedback.incorrect_en: 買う (buy) doesn't apply to people; 頼め would need a different particle (に) and shifts the nuance.

contrast_examples.jp: ベビーシッターを雇う。

prompt.context_jp: natsumiが桑野に反撃する場面:
prompt.prompt_jp: 余計な___です。
prompt.prompt_en: Common comeback: 'none of your business'

feedback.correct_en: 余計なお世話 is the set phrase meaning 'that's unwanted meddling / none of your business.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 余計な仕事 means 'extra work'; 余計な問題 means 'unnecessary problem' — neither is the retort here.

prompt.context_jp: 桑野が自信満々に言う:
prompt.prompt_en: 'Piece of cake / easy win' — which word?

feedback.correct_en: 楽勝 (らくしょう) = easy victory, used casually to mean 'piece of cake.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 楽観 is 'optimism' (abstract); 気楽 is 'carefree' — neither fits this confident boast.

prompt.context_jp: 「夜10時過ぎると 霊が出るから___よ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 気を___よ。
prompt.prompt_en: 'Be careful' — which verb?

feedback.correct_en: 気をつける = be careful. Imperative is 気をつけろ.
feedback.incorrect_en: 気を持つ isn't a fixed phrase for caution; 気を入れる means 'put effort in,' not 'watch out.'

prompt.context_jp: 桑野は英治に雑用を___とした。
prompt.prompt_jp: 桑野は英治に雑用を___とした。
prompt.prompt_en: 'tried to ask for a chore' — which verb?

feedback.correct_en: 〜に〜を頼む = ask someone to do something. Volitional 頼もう fits 'tried to ask.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 願う is more formal/grand (like making a wish/request formally); 聞く wouldn't fit the sense of delegating a chore.

prompt.context_jp: 「今やってる仕事も ちょうど___ですし」
prompt.prompt_jp: ちょうど___です。
prompt.prompt_en: 'at the critical peak' — which word?

feedback.correct_en: ヤマ場 = the climax / critical peak of a task or event.
feedback.incorrect_en: 現場 is 'the site/scene'; 本場 is 'home of / authentic place' — neither means climax.

prompt.context_jp: 「やるっつったら やるんだよ ___ことすんなよ！」
prompt.prompt_jp: ___ことすんなよ！
prompt.prompt_en: 'Don't do unnecessary things!' — which word fits?

feedback.correct_en: 余計なことする = to meddle / do unnecessary things, Kuwano's angry retort.
feedback.incorrect_en: 大事な (important) or 簡単な (easy) wouldn't convey annoyance at interference.

prompt.context_jp: Kuwano shouts in anger at Maya and Eiji:
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural as an angry outburst telling them to leave?

choices.text: いることないだろう、出てけ！
いる必要がないでしょう、出ていってください。

feedback.correct_en: The drama's blunt, casual tone of anger calls for 出てけ with dropped particles and the colloquial ないだろう.
feedback.incorrect_en: Option B is too polite/measured for a shouted outburst in a heated argument.

contrast_examples.jp: お帰りいただけますか。

prompt.context_jp: Natsumi offers leftovers to Kuwano over the intercom:
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds more natural for 'if you'd like, do you want some?'

choices.text: よかったら要りません？
良いならば必要ですか？

feedback.correct_en: よかったら…要りません？ is natural casual Japanese for offering something.
feedback.incorrect_en: 良いならば…必要ですか is stiff and bookish — nobody offers food like that.

contrast_examples.en: Want to eat (this), if you'd like?

contrast_examples.jp: もしよろしければ、いかがですか。
contrast_examples.en: If you don't mind, would you like some? (polite)

prompt.context_jp: Kuwano explains why he didn't greet Natsumi:
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds more natural?

choices.text: 話しかけて話題がなかったら、イヤでしょう？
話をして内容が存在しなかった場合、嫌悪ですか？

feedback.correct_en: The conversational 〜たら、…でしょう？ pattern matches Kuwano's dry, everyday speech.
feedback.incorrect_en: Option B uses stiff, legalistic vocabulary (存在しなかった場合, 嫌悪) that no one would say in conversation.

contrast_examples.jp: 話題がなかったら気まずいでしょう。
contrast_examples.en: It'd be awkward with no topic, right?

contrast_examples.jp: 話題が存在しない場合、不快である。
contrast_examples.en: In the event of no topic existing, it is unpleasant. (unnatural)

prompt.context_jp: Maya teasing Kuwano about declining the job:
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural in Maya's teasing, informal tone?

choices.text: ムリなら しょうがないわね
不可能であれば仕方がございません

feedback.correct_en: ムリなら…わね is natural casual female speech Maya uses to tease Kuwano.
feedback.incorrect_en: 不可能であれば…ございません is overly formal — totally mismatched with their office banter.

contrast_examples.en: If it's impossible, it can't be helped. (casual)

contrast_examples.jp: ご無理でしたら致し方ございません。
contrast_examples.en: If it proves impossible, it cannot be helped. (very formal)

prompt.context_jp: Natsumi to a stubborn Kuwano:
prompt.prompt_en: Which is the natural way to say 'why don't you just give up (resign yourself)?'

choices.text: いいかげん観念したらどうですか？
適度に諦めを認識するのはどうですか？

feedback.correct_en: いいかげん…したらどうですか？ with 観念する is the natural, idiomatic way to urge someone to stop resisting.
feedback.incorrect_en: Option B is a word-salad calque — no native speaker constructs it that way.
